einzeiler: How to make your home reflect your true personality without spending a lot of money.
kurzfassung: Cass interviews interior designer Olivia Westbrooks about making homes reflect personal identity rather than generic trends. They discuss overcoming perfectionism, starting big dreams with small, imperfect steps, and letting go of the fear of judgment. The episode also features listener questions on organizing small multi-purpose spaces and navigating ADHD in relationships.
stichpunkte: Olivia Westbrooks shares her journey as an interior designer and her experience filming the Hallmark show Home is Where the Heart Is.
The hosts discuss how homes often lack personal reflection due to following trends and catering to outside expectations.
Olivia and Cass explore the paralyzing effects of perfectionism and why doing things poorly on purpose helps break mental blocks.
Starting small with creative outlets, such as painting or launching a podcast, builds confidence and momentum.
Olivia advises creating a vision or mood board as a foundational step to uncover personal style and color preferences.
Cass shares practical ideas for incorporating personal history into living spaces, such as displaying love letters or meaningful keepsakes.
In the listener Q&A, Cass addresses organizing small multi-purpose rooms using sketching, prioritization, and the container concept.
Listeners share personal stories about finding inspiration, overcoming fear, and recognizing ADHD traits in partners.

clips.hook: How an interior designer landed a television show through a simple email.
clips.text: Olivia explains that she secured her role on a television show after receiving an unexpected email from casting directors.

clips.hook: Cass humorously questions the prerequisites for entering the medical field.
clips.text: Cass jokes about wanting a doctorate to perform surgery without having to go through schooling or actually do the hard work.

clips.hook: The reminder that nobody starts out great and early attempts are usually bad.
clips.text: Olivia points out that every successful professional in any field begins with poor results and has to build their skills like a muscle.

clips.hook: Why perfectionists should try doing things badly on purpose.
clips.text: Olivia suggests giving perfectionists intentional challenges, like doing tasks poorly on purpose, to prove that the world will not end.

clips.hook: Cass hilariously debates whether she is frugal or simply cheap.
clips.text: Cass admits to being exceptionally cheap when buying home decor items rather than being intentionally frugal.

beschreibung:
Want interior design tips that actually reflect your personal style — not just another Pinterest trend? In this episode, I talk home decor, storytelling through design, and chasing big dreams with Olivia Westbrooks, interior designer and star of Hallmark's Home Is Where the Heart Is.

Olivia has been designing for over 22 years, and after her show gave her a taste of what's possible, she got real with me about what came next . . . and why she finally pulled her podcast equipment out of the box after three years of letting it collect dust (be honest, is yours still in the box too?).

We get into:

✨ Why the best-designed homes tell a story instead of following a trend

✨ How to figure out your personal style when you don't even know where to start

✨ Why doing something badly on purpose might be the fastest way through perfectionism

✨ Small, low-cost ways to make your space feel more like you today — no renovation required

✨ The moment Olivia posted her most "imperfect" video ever... and it became her best-performing post

If you've ever shoved a dream to the bottom of your list because life got busy, or you're stuck buying stuff that never quite feels you, this conversation is your permission slip to take one small, brave step today.
